[[Persepolis F.C.|Persepolis]] were the [[2019–20 Persian Gulf Pro League|defending champions]]. The season featured 14 teams from the [[2019–20 Persian Gulf Pro League]] and two new teams promoted from the [[2019–20 Azadegan League]]: [[Mes Rafsanjan F.C.|Mes Rafsanjan]] and [[Aluminium Arak F.C.|Aluminium Arak]].{{Cite web |date=2020-08-17 |title=Aluminium Arak secure promotion to IPL |url=https://www.tehrantimes.com/news/451339/Aluminium-Arak-secure-promotion-to-IPL |access-date=2020-09-01}}{{Cite web |date=2020-08-02 |title=Mes Rafsanjan promoted to Iran Professional League |url=https://www.tehrantimes.com/news/450806/Mes-Rafsanjan-promoted-to-Iran-Professional-League |access-date=2020-09-01}} The 2020–21 season started on 6 November 2020 and was ended on 30 July 2021.{{Cite web |date=2020-11-01 |title=2020/21 IPL to kick off as scheduled: official |url=https://www.tehrantimes.com/news/454162/2020-21-IPL-to-kick-off-as-scheduled-official |access-date=2020-11-06}} [[Persepolis F.C.|Persepolis]] won their record-extending 5th consecutive title and 14th title overall (7th in the Pro League era) == Teams == === Stadia and locations === {{#invoke:Transcludable section|main|section=map|text= {{Location map+|Iran|width=400|float=right|caption=Locations of clubs in 2020–21 Persian Gulf Pro League|places={{Location map~ |Iran |marksize=18 |lat=35.69611 |long=51.42306 |label= }} {{Location map~ |Iran |marksize=9 |lat=30.80 |long=56.50 |label=[[Mes Rafsanjan F.C.|Mes Rafsanjan]]|position=top}} {{Location map~ |Iran |marksize=9 |lat=29.275 |long=55.80 |label=[[Gol Gohar Sirjan F.C.|Gol Gohar]]|position=right}} {{Location map~ |Iran |marksize=9|lat=31.32750 |long=48.69389 |label=[[Foolad F.C.|Foolad]]|position=right}} {{Location map~ |Iran |marksize=9 |lat=34.50 |long=49.99 |label=[[Aluminium Arak F.C.|Aluminium Arak]]|position=bottom}} {{Location map~ |Iran |marksize=12 |lat=32.63333 |long=51.65000 |label=[[Sepahan F.C.|Sepahan]]
